title: ProtoRAIL: A Risk-cognizant Imitation Agent for Adaptive vCPU Oversubscription In the Cloud
problem: Cloud vCPU oversubscription policies must jointly minimize overloading risk (hot nodes) and maximize utilization (stranded resource recovery), but demand patterns vary dynamically across VM types and time, making static heuristic policies either too conservative (waste capacity) or too aggressive (cause overload).
method: ProtoRAIL has three components: (1) Prototypical Imitation Learning - a trajectory encoder (LSTM or Transformer) maps CPU usage trajectories to embeddings; K prototype embeddings represent equivalence classes of usage patterns; policy is a linear layer over similarities to prototypes. Loss has four terms: Lrep (representativeness: L2 distance to nearest prototype), Ldiv (diversity: repel close prototypes), Lint (interpretability: anchor each prototype to a real trajectory), and LIMloss (imitation learning via behavior cloning or adversarial IL). (2) Active Knowledge-in-the-Loop (KITL) - identifies uncertain prototypes (high cluster entropy) and risky predictions (predicted oversubscription rate below actual usage) via a query framework; solicits feedback from domain experts (or LLMs) as up/down votes on prototypes and actions, plus merge/split operations on prototype clusters; feedback is applied via advice potential gates (exponential scaling of loss components) to steer training without explicit prior design. (3) Query scheduling - minimizes feedback budget by only querying at uncertain or risky stages.

title: N:M Sparse DNN Kernels for RISC-V MCUs via Custom ISA Extension
problem: N:M semi-structured sparsity cannot be efficiently exploited on RISC-V microcontrollers (MCUs) because standard ISAs lack the hardware primitives to accelerate structured sparse operations without prohibitive overhead.
method: A custom xDecimate ISA instruction is added to a RISC-V core that performs hardware-accelerated N:M sparse selection and MAC in a single operation. Decimate Im2col reformulates convolution to enable xDecimate on im2col-transformed feature maps. The MATCH compiler generates xDecimate-aware kernels. Synthesized at 22nm targeting the Vega PULP SoC (basis for commercial GAP9). Evaluated on ResNet-18 and ViT at 1:4, 1:8, and 1:16 sparsity ratios.

title: Characterizing and Optimizing Realistic Workloads on a Commercial Compute-in-SRAM Device
problem: Prior compute-in-SRAM evaluations rely on simulators or small prototypes, so the real-world performance and energy efficiency of commercial devices under realistic AI workloads (particularly retrieval-augmented generation over large corpora) is not well understood, and programming principles for exploiting the architecture's 2-million bit-processor parallelism are largely unknown.
method: The paper characterizes the commercial GSI APU (2M 1-bit processors at 500 MHz, 25 TOPS, 26 TB/s on-chip bandwidth, 12MB L1 / 64KB L2 / 1MB L3 / 16GB DDR) using the Phoenix benchmark suite and matrix multiplication microbenchmarks, and develops a Python-based analytical framework modeling non-uniform data movement costs across 4 memory levels (L1-L4) and intra-VR vs. inter-VR operations. Three optimizations are proposed and validated on real hardware: (1) communication-aware reduction mapping that maps the reduction axis temporally to cheaper inter-VR operations (scalar-vector product) rather than costly intra-VR spatial reduction; (2) DMA coalescing via subgroup copy to eliminate redundant off-chip data duplication across loop iterations; and (3) broadcast-friendly data layouts that reduce L3 lookup table sizes from K*N to N elements to cut broadcast latency. These optimizations are applied to RAG retrieval over 10-200GB corpora.

title: COMET: Fine-grained Computation-communication Overlapping for Mixture-of-Experts
problem: In distributed MoE models, inter-device all-to-all communication occupies up to 47% of total execution time. Existing coarse-grained overlapping schemes impair computational efficiency and provide sub-optimal latency concealment.
method: COMET introduces two mechanisms: (1) Shared Tensor Based Dependency Resolving: analyzes the shared buffers between producer (communication) and consumer (computation) operations, decomposes shared tensors along independent dimensions (M-axis for layer0 GEMM, N-axis for layer1 top-K reduction), and reschedules computation tiles to begin as early as possible using local data first. (2) Adaptive Workload Assignment: thread-block specialization isolates communication and computation in separate SM groups within a fused kernel, with adaptive thread-block allocation profiled per input shape and parallelism strategy.

title: DarwinGame: Playing Tournaments for Tuning Applications in Noisy Cloud Environments
problem: Existing application performance tuners (OpenTuner, ActiveHarmony, BLISS) implicitly assume a dedicated interference-free execution environment; when used as-is in shared cloud environments with unpredictable co-tenant interference, they produce suboptimal tuning configurations that are more than 40% away from optimal because interference levels differ across configuration evaluations, causing the tuner to misrank configurations.
method: DarwinGame is a tournament-based tuner that bypasses the inability to control cloud interference by co-locating multiple copies of the same application with different tuning configurations on the same VM, exposing all competing configurations to identical interference conditions simultaneously. Tournaments are structured across four phases: (1) Regional phase (Swiss-style): the search space is divided into 10,000 regions; configurations within each region compete in parallel with early termination when a clear winner emerges based on work-done execution score; (2) Global phase (double-elimination style): regional winners compete with losers given a second chance, with both execution score and consistency score (average 1/rank across games) used for judging; (3) Playoffs (barrage style): top survivors compete two-at-a-time without early termination; (4) Final: two finalists compete to produce the winning configuration. This multi-phase design identifies configurations with both low execution time and low performance variability under interference.
